subject: Joe Biden considered pardoning Trump during 2023 pillow talk with Jill, GOP governor says
posts:
Behind closed doors in 2023, Joe Biden mulled a Trump pardon to lower national tension.
Evidence: Bedtime talk, GOP governor's book, no pardon issued
#Aletheia #USPol

Biden reportedly weighed a pardon for Donald Trump to ease political turmoil, as revealed in Gov. Spencer Cox's new book.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Good Preference

While floated as a peace gesture, the maneuver highlights elite bargaining above public accountability.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Private flirtation with pardons exposes backroom political trade-offs masquerading as noble unity.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 4.5, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Gov. Spencer Cox: PASS (0.5, 0.4) — Highlights private talks for peace.
- Biden Administration: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Elite calculus over open justice.
Utah Gov. Spencer Cox revealed in his upcoming book that he urged Biden to pardon Trump in August 2023 to deescalate national tensions, prompting Biden to admit he and Jill discussed it.

The Bright Side:
At least high-level leaders acknowledged the corrosive nature of endless partisan prosecutions, even if acting on it proved politically impossible.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (a legal prosecution of a candidate) with WHO (elite political self-preservation), ignoring systemic public trust.

Social Physics Analysis:
Power protects power under the guise of peace. Rather than letting transparent legal processes play out, elites toy with backroom clemency to manage political fallout.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Private backroom deals erode public faith in equal justice.

The Unavoidable Truth: Leaders privately recognize that intense political prosecutions tear the nation apart.

The Unavoidable Lie: Floating pardons behind closed doors constitutes genuine bipartisan statesmanship.

Alethekanon:
Private clemency musings expose the fragility of rule of law when elite self-preservation trumps public accountability.

Awwthekanon:
It is exhausting to watch power structure itself around shielding elites while ordinary people bear the weight of the system.

Brothekanon:
Wild that Biden and Jill were pillow-talking about pardoning Trump while the indictments were literally rolling in.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not pervert justice; do not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the great, but judge your neighbor fairly." Leviticus 19:15 PASS
True peace requires equal justice, not backroom elite pardons.
